From: Anika Roy <security@cloudlinehealth.com>

Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Short-term cross-region processing during DR test (ask & proof)

Hi Marissa,

Quick note from Cloudline InfoSec — we're about to run a DR failover exercise next month that will briefly route encrypted inference traffic through Redwood's us-east and eu-west regions for up to 48 hours. We need 1) formal confirmation of the temporary cross-region processing window, 2) a short checklist of controls (key custody, access audit trail, temporary subprocessor activation list), and 3) an ops contact for the exact start/end times so our runbook can tie to your logs.

Specifically we need:
- A statement that data will be processed only for the stated 48h window and returned to EU-only placement afterwards.
- Details on KMS key handling (who holds keys during the window; any transient key export?).
- Which subprocessors will be activated and their country-of-processing.
- Sample audit entries we can expect (log fields and retention).

Attached is our DR questionnaire (Cloudline_DQ_Checklist_v1.xlsx). Would prefer answers by EOD Monday so we can finalize our runbook.

Thanks —
Anika Roy
Head of Security, Cloudline Health

Anika — thanks for the clear checklist. Looping in Diego (Ops) and Jonas (Legal) for the operational and contractual bits. High-level answers below; we'll follow with a short checklist doc and a proposed telemetry sample.

Short answers up front:
- Temporary window: Redwood can authorize a scheduled 48-hour cross-region processing window. We will return to EU-only placement once the window closes and validate placement via telemetry.
- KMS: keys remain in customer-side KMS when you use an external key option. For Cloudline's current setup (Redwood-managed KMS), we will create a short-lived key wrapping policy for the DR window; no key material is exported from our HSMs.
- Subprocessors: We'll provide a temporary activation roster (names + locations). A short list will be submitted — in most cases the activated infra is our existing fleet in us-east and eu-west (no third-party data processors beyond our cloud infra partners).
- Audit entries: we'll send a sample log extract (timestamp, request_id, region, model, bytes_processed, action, operator_id).

Next steps: Diego, can you prepare the ops checklist and the sample telemetry? Jonas, can you confirm whether the DPA needs a signed addendum for this window or if our standard transient-processing clause suffices?

Marissa
Account Lead — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: subprocessor_roster.csv (text/csv) — preliminary list]

Thanks Marissa. Draft ops checklist and telemetry sample below — attaching the CSV roster we plan to use to activate the nodes. This is operational only; no new subprocessors beyond our cloud infra partners.

Planned runbook items (operational checklist):
1) Pre-window verification (24h before): confirm build-id and node list for eu-west primary and us-east standby.
2) KMS handling: create ephemeral key-wrap policy; keys remain in HSM; no raw key export. Key wrapping uses AES-256-GCM and audit entry on wrap/ununwrap.
3) Route activation: feature-flag to enable cross-region routing; exact start timestamp will be scheduled ISO time.
4) Telemetry & logs: enable request-level trace for DR window with retention set to 90 days for these entries; sample fields provided below.
5) Post-window validation (within 4h): run placement verification, purge transient caches, rotate ephemeral policies.
6) Evidence package: we produce an ops report and a signed statement of placement for your compliance archive.

Telemetry sample (CSV format):
- timestamp, request_id, user_hash, region_processed, node_id, model_id, token_count, action, operator_id, retention_flag

Attachments: subprocessor_roster.csv (prelim)

Let me know proposed start window and I'll lock nodes and provide single-run logs after the test.

Diego

Marissa / Anika — legal flags and suggested language below. Short answer: Cloudline and Redwood should sign a one-off addendum that references the DR window and the evidence package. Our standard transient-processing clause covers short automatic failovers, but a scheduled cross-region run tied to a customer test is better with an explicit addendum to avoid any ambiguity for auditors.

Suggested addendum bullets (legal):
- Purpose & window: define start/end timestamps (UTC) and max duration (48 hours).
- Data scope: confirms subset of requests only (production inference traffic explicitly listed if needed).
- Key custody: states no export of key material; ephemeral key policy duration and operator list.
- Subprocessors: specify that no new third-party processors will be engaged during the window, and list cloud infra partners as required.
- Evidence & audit: Redwood will provide the ops report (signed), sample logs, and a placement statement within 72 hours of window close.
- Liability carveouts: limited to documented procedural negligence during the scheduled window.

If you want, I can draft an addendum template for signatures today. Marissa — if Cloudline prefers we can embed the narrow window language as an exhibit to the DPA rather than a standalone addendum.

Jonas Weber
Counsel — Redwood Inference
